citation: StataCorp, Stata Base Reference Manual, [R] ologit, Example 1, p. 4 (https://www.stata.com/manuals/rologit.pdf; release 19). The page prints the whole dataset as the cross-tabulation `tabulate rep77 foreign`: rep77 Poor 2 domestic and 1 foreign, Fair 10 and 1, Average 20 and 7, Good 13 and 7, Excellent 0 and 5, totalling 45 domestic, 21 foreign and 66 cars. The repair records are the 1977 wave of the 1978 Automobile Data described in [U] 1.2.2 Example datasets.
notes:
THE COLUMN MARGIN OF THE SAME PUBLISHED CROSS-TABULATION, one row per car, in the same order as its companion stata_r_ologit_1977_repair_record: within each repair record the domestic cars come first, coded 0, then the foreign ones, coded 1. It sums to 21 foreign cars over 66, which is the column total the page prints.

IT IS A FRAME AND NOT A SERIES because the node it is written for takes its covariates as a table; one column is the whole design the published fit uses, which is what makes the printed coefficient and the four printed cut points reproducible from this page alone.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPORT. Origin of manufacture is the only covariate the page publishes a fit for. The cell it leaves empty -- no domestic car has an Excellent 1977 record -- is a property of the data rather than a defect in it, and it is what makes the fourth dichotomy 1{rep77 > 4} separate; a test of proportional odds over this design has no maximum-likelihood estimate to build its fourth binary fit from.
